clue.text: A pole, a pole, a pole, a fruit

parts.note: N, for north, is one of the two magnetic poles
N again, the north pole
S, for south, is the other pole

explanation.surface: A chant-like list of poles that ends, absurdly, in a piece of fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: The repeated 'a pole' is a chain of separate pieces: each 'a' gives A and the three poles give N, N and S in turn. The last 'a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the pineapple's name in French and several other languages, used in English too for the tropical fruit.

clue.text: I may be cagey if Gardner's attorney is taxed

parts.note: Ava Gardner was the Hollywood film star
DA is a district attorney, the American public prosecutor
VAT, value added tax, is the British sales tax, so goods that are taxed carry it

explanation.surface: A film star's lawyer complains that he is being taxed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I may be cagey' is the bird speaking: it is a small finch commonly kept in cages. VAT is the British tax added to goods, value added tax.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a red munia of South Asia, a popular cage bird, so it is a creature that may be kept caged.

clue.text: Articles on Northern Ireland, one by a Greek

parts.note: A and THE are the indefinite and definite articles
an means one, as in an apple

explanation.surface: Reports on Northern Ireland, one of them written by a Greek journalist.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' puts the articles above the next piece, so they come first.
explanation.definitionFit: A citizen of Athens is a Greek, so the city's people serve as an example of Greeks.

clue.text: Bar put out by the unexpected

indicators.note: out here means put out of order, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A pub rule is upset by something nobody saw coming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' asks for BARPUT to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sudden and without warning is unexpected, as an abrupt halt is.

clue.text: Beast opposing what Spielberg lost after Rada fiasco

indicators.note: after means the opposing piece and the Spielberg piece follow the jumbled drama school
a fiasco is a mess, so the letters of the word are in disarray

parts.note: V is short for versus, against or opposing
Spielberg directed Raiders of the Lost Ark, so the thing lost is the ark

explanation.surface: An animal stands against the film director's lost property after a drama school disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: The drama school is RADA, the Royal Academy of Dramatic Art in London; 'fiasco' jumbles its letters and 'after' sets the other pieces behind them. Spielberg made Raiders of the Lost Ark.
explanation.definitionFit: The aardvark is an African burrowing mammal, so it is an animal, a beast.

clue.text: Part of (perhaps early) building

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A section of a building that may date from an early period.
explanation.definitionFit: An apse is the rounded end of a church, and the clue loosely calls that structure a building.

clue.text: What does an iron do? Get less

definitions.meaning: an iron takes the wrinkles out of cloth, read here as un-wrinkle

explanation.definitionFit: To shrink is to diminish, and read as de-crease it is to remove wrinkles as an iron does.

clue.text: Group formed by a cat, one with its first baby?

parts.note: a tom is a male cat
I is the Roman numeral one
C stands for cum, Latin for with, as in prescriptions
a cat's young is called a kitten

explanation.surface: A family of cats is formed when a tom and a mate have their first offspring.
explanation.walkthrough: C for 'with' comes from the Latin cum, abbreviated c in old prescriptions. The question mark signals that 'Group' is a pop band, not a gathering of cats.
explanation.definitionFit: Atomic Kitten were a British girl band of the early 2000s, a pop group.

clue.text: See 7
Stick commercial at this point

parts.note: an ad is a commercial, a television advertisement
here means at this point or place

explanation.surface: A notice telling you to post an advertisement in this spot.
explanation.definitionFit: To adhere is to cling or remain attached, as glue holds things together.

clue.text: Stage dame put tree on smallholding

parts.note: the ash is a common tree
a croft is a small Scottish farm or smallholding

explanation.surface: A gardener plants a tree on a small farm.
explanation.walkthrough: A croft is a small rented farm in the Scottish Highlands.
explanation.definitionFit: Dame Peggy Ashcroft was an English actress honoured as a dame for her work in theatre.

clue.text: A soldier leads a painter in nimble style

parts.note: GI is an American soldier
Sir Peter Lely was the Dutch-born portrait painter at the court of Charles II

explanation.surface: A soldier is out in front of an artist as they both move quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leads' places the soldier ahead of the painter.
explanation.definitionFit: To move with agility is to move nimbly, so the adverb means in a nimble manner.

clue.text: Merry wife's daughter takes a long time to go round airless planet

indicators.note: to go round means one piece surrounds the other, so the remaining letters sit inside

parts.note: an age is a long time

indicators.note: an air is a tune, so taking the air away removes those letters

parts.note: Neptune is the eighth planet

explanation.surface: A joyful woman's daughter spends ages circling a planet with no atmosphere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Merry' is Shakespeare's title, not cheerfulness. An air is a tune, so 'airless' strips that from the planet to leave NEP, which 'to go round' places inside the long time.
explanation.definitionFit: In Shakespeare's The Merry Wives of Windsor, Mistress Page has a daughter called Anne.

clue.text: Brought back from Spain the concept of a Roman official

indicators.note: brought back says the whole sequence is read backwards

parts.note: el is Spanish for the
an idea is a concept

explanation.surface: A traveller returns from Spain with a new idea about Roman officials.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brought back' turns ELIDEA around as a whole.
explanation.definitionFit: An aedile was a magistrate in ancient Rome in charge of public buildings and games.

clue.text: Bill at eating place can be staged

parts.note: AC is an account, which is a bill
a table is where one eats

explanation.surface: Someone named Bill, at a restaurant table, wonders if a play could be put on.
explanation.definitionFit: A play that can be performed in a theatre is fit to act.

clue.text: Open for a spot of liquid refreshment…

parts.note: a jar is British slang for a drink, especially of beer

explanation.surface: A pub is open for a quick drink.
explanation.walkthrough: A jar is British slang for a glass of beer.
explanation.definitionFit: A door left slightly open is said to be ajar.

clue.text: which is how much with a herb?

parts.note: which refers back to the liquid refreshment of the previous clue, read as ale
cost asks how much something is

explanation.surface: Continuing from the last clue, a drinker asks what the price is with a herb added.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis joins this clue to the one before: 'which' stands for the refreshment there, here ALE.
explanation.definitionFit: Alecost, also called costmary, is an aromatic plant once used to flavour beer.

clue.text: Executioner about to permit Sappers to separate revolutionary elements

indicators.note: about means the executioner's tool goes around the other pieces

parts.note: the axe is the executioner's tool, standing for the executioner
let means permit or allow
RE is the Royal Engineers, the British Army's sappers

explanation.surface: The executioner is about to let some soldiers break up a group of rebels.
explanation.walkthrough: The Royal Engineers, the British Army's engineering corps, are known as the Sappers. 'about' puts LETRE inside AXE.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a fixed bar on which wheels turn, keeping the two rotating parts apart.

clue.text: Sailor finds reader wandering in Welsh town

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is a sailor

indicators.note: wandering letters stray from their places, so the letters of the word are rearranged

explanation.surface: A seaman meets someone reading as he roams a town in Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wandering' rearranges READER to ERDARE.
explanation.definitionFit: Aberdare is a town in the Cynon Valley in south Wales.

clue.text: Burns home and cattle

definitions.meaning: the region where the poet Robert Burns was born and lived
a Scottish breed of dairy cattle

explanation.definitionFit: This Scottish county was Robert Burns's birthplace and gives its name to a dairy breed of cows.

clue.text: A cricket team with everyone backward point is the pits

parts.note: a cricket team has eleven players, XI in Roman numerals

indicators.note: backward says the word for everyone is read in reverse

parts.note: all means everyone
E, east, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A cricket side with every fielder at backward point is hopeless.
explanation.walkthrough: Backward point is a cricket fielding position, but here 'backward' turns ALL into LLA. 'the pits' are armpits.
explanation.definitionFit: These are the Latin plural for the armpits, the hollows under the arms.

clue.text: A Blyton character displayed with skill

indicators.note: the run of characters is shown inside the words, so the letters are found in them

explanation.surface: One of Enid Blyton's characters is shown off with skill.
explanation.walkthrough: Enid Blyton was a British children's author; the letters sit inside 'A Blyton'.
explanation.definitionFit: To do something capably is to do it with skill.

clue.text: A lasting pain at North German city

parts.note: an ache is a persistent pain

explanation.surface: A persistent pain troubles a traveller in a city in northern Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: Aachen is a city in western Germany, once Charlemagne's capital.

clue.text: A heartless minister of gion has a number like other numbers

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'A heartless minister of gion has a number like other numbers': OCR dropped letters (likely 'religion'); wordplay A + RA(B)BI + C needs them, no scan available
annotationWithheld.clue: A heartless minister of gion has a number like other numbers

clue.text: Shelter for a year in a squalid area

indicators.note: in means the year is placed inside the squalid area

parts.note: a slum is a squalid area of a town

explanation.surface: Someone seeks a roof for a year in a run-down part of town.
explanation.definitionFit: Asylum is protection or refuge, a place of shelter.

clue.text: "The Angel of Death" shows misplaced zeal engulfing painter

indicators.note: engulfing means the rearranged letters surround the painter
misplaced letters are out of their places, so the word is rearranged

parts.note: RA, Royal Academician, is a painter

explanation.surface: Death's angel displays enthusiasm gone wrong, swallowing an artist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misplaced' gives AZEL, and 'engulfing' wraps that around the painter. RA stands for Royal Academician, a member of the Royal Academy of Arts.
explanation.definitionFit: In Jewish and Islamic tradition Azrael is the angel who separates souls from bodies.

clue.text: Was it liquorice that made the world?

definitions.text: Was it liquorice that made the world?

parts.words: Was it liquorice that made the world?
parts.note: plays on the saying that it takes all kinds to make a world, joined to a mixed bag of liquorice sweets

explanation.definitionFit: Liquorice allsorts are mixed sweets, and the proverb says it takes every type to make a world.

clue.text: Scots own university first Japanese

parts.note: ain is Scots for own

explanation.surface: A Scot owns the university that comes first in Japan.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ainu are the indigenous people of northern Japan, who lived there before the Japanese.

clue.text: Greeting to Swiss city — I take one from Ireland

parts.note: hi is a greeting
Bern is the Swiss capital
a means one

explanation.surface: Saying hello to a Swiss city, a traveller accepts a visitor from Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: This was the Latin name the Romans gave to Ireland.

clue.text: You don't want acid, it's a student destroyer

parts.note: L for learner, as on a learner driver's plate
Kali is the Hindu goddess of destruction

explanation.surface: Someone warns against acid, calling a student a wrecker.
explanation.walkthrough: L is the learner's plate on British cars, so it stands for a student.
explanation.definitionFit: A base is the chemical opposite of an acid, so it is what you want when you don't want acid.

clue.text: Sense outside the area of Purley, as it's said

indicators.note: outside means the word for sense goes around the area

parts.note: nous is common sense
an acre is a unit of area

explanation.surface: Someone with sense lives just beyond the suburb of Purley.
explanation.walkthrough: Purley is a suburb of south London; said aloud it sounds like pearly, the real definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Mother-of-pearl is nacre, so something like it is pearly.

clue.text: A representative before the current one?

parts.note: an MP, Member of Parliament, represents a constituency
ere means before

explanation.surface: Is a former MP the predecessor of the present holder?
explanation.walkthrough: 'current' looks like 'present', but the definition is a unit of electric current.
explanation.definitionFit: The amp is the SI unit of electrical current.
